title: Ohn No Khao Swè (Burmese Coconut Chicken Noodles)
summary: Chicken thighs simmer in a coconut milk and gram flour broth spiced with turmeric, paprika and chilli, served over egg noodles with egg, crispy noodles and lime.
equipment: large heavy saucepan or casserole (24-26 cm, 4 litres)

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 2 cm pieces

ingredients.note: to season at the end, to taste

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon of fish sauce and the turmeric, and leave for 15 minutes to pick up colour and seasoning before it goes into the pot.

steps.title: Toast the gram flour
steps.text: Toast the gram flour in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and a shade darker - this removes its raw, beany taste. Whisk it with 150ml of the stock to make a smooth slurry.

steps.title: Build the broth base
steps.text: Heat the oil in the saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 8-10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1-2 minutes, then the paprika and chilli for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and stir for 2-3 minutes until coated in the spices and no longer pink on the outside. Pour in the remaining stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Thicken and add coconut milk
steps.text: Whisk in the gram flour slurry and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. Add the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes - keep the heat low rather than boiling hard, or the coconut milk can split - until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Season and cook the noodles
steps.text: Stir in the remaining fish sauce to taste. Cook the egg noodles according to the packet, drain, and divide between bowls.

steps.title: Assemble and serve
steps.text: Ladle the broth and chicken over the noodles, then top each bowl with egg halves, red onion, crispy fried noodles, coriander and a pinch of chilli flakes. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

tips: Toast the gram flour until fragrant before mixing it with stock - skipping this leaves a raw, chalky taste in the broth.
Common mistake: boiling the soup hard once the coconut milk goes in, which can cause it to split. Keep it at a gentle simmer from that point on.
Season with fish sauce gradually and taste as you go, since the right amount varies by brand.
Add the crispy noodles just before serving so they stay crunchy rather than softening in the broth.
Cook the egg noodles separately and add the broth at the table if you're not serving everyone right away, to stop them turning soft.
storage: Store the broth and noodles separately in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat the broth gently on the hob, stirring, until piping hot throughout (74°C (165°F)), and cook fresh noodles rather than reheating them in the broth. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour on a day above 32°C (90°F)).
